paragraphs:
The Defender Octa is the flagship performance variant of the modern L663 Defender, launched in 2024. At its heart sits the BMW S68B44T0 — a 4.4-litre twin-turbocharged V8. This is the only BMW-sourced engine in the Defender range, sharing its basic architecture with BMW's S63/N63 hot-vee family but featuring a cross-plane crank and mild-hybrid assistance.

The Octa represents a significant departure from the rest of the Defender powertrain line-up — it's not an Ingenium-based unit, and it has its own distinct characteristics, including a 48V mild-hybrid system that's BMW's own hardware, separate from the Ingenium MHEV system used elsewhere in the range.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace S68B44T0 engines for every Defender Octa on the road.

cards.body: A 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 fitted to the Defender Octa from 2024 to present (L663 generation). BMW's latest performance V8 architecture, featuring a hot-vee design with turbos positioned between the cylinder banks. compatibility.intro: The S68B44T0 is a specialised engine unique to the Octa within the Land Rover range. It's not interchangeable with the AJ133 supercharged V8 used in other Defender V8 variants (P425/P500/P525), nor with any Ingenium diesel or petrol units. When we quote or supply any work on a Defender Octa, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (S68B44T0) via registration or VIN
BMW-sourced hardware considerations specific to this engine

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Defender quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
